value.title: Docs in the pij CLI: the start page, docs list and docs get
value.summary: PRD 009 workstream step s01. Two pij-rs verbs, `agents-start-here` and `docs` (`list`, `get <page>[#<heading>]`), print markdown pages compiled into the binary from `docs/cli/`. They run before the runtime and client exist: no daemon, no network, no child process. The pij shim forwards both.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: pij refuses `pij docs` today, and a seat outside the pij repo cannot read `docs/how/`. Pages now live as markdown files in `docs/cli/` (page id = path without `.md`, so a later `types/knowledge` page is a file in `docs/cli/types/`). One table in a pure module, `crates/cli/src/docs.rs`, includes each file with `include_str!`, so the pages are fixed at build time with the version. The first page is the start page; the concepts and type pages follow in step s03 by adding files and table rows.

sections.name: goals
value: Any seat in any repo reads pij's start page and reference pages with one command.
The pages a seat reads match the pij binary it runs.

sections.name: non_goals
value: The concepts, type and pods pages (step s03) and the check that a bundled page equals its file (step s02).
Refusals and first turns naming pages (step s04).

value.claim: `pij agents-start-here` prints the start page (what pij is, how a seat learns who it is and who governs it, the first commands to run, pointers to existing docs) and exits 0 with no daemon. `--json` prints it in the usual envelope.

`pij docs list` names every bundled page with its one-line summary. `pij docs get <page>` prints the whole page; `pij docs get <page>#<heading>` prints only that section (the heading to the next heading of the same or higher level), the heading matched by its text or its slug, case-insensitive. An unknown page or heading refuses (exit 2) naming the nearest page or heading and `pij docs list`.
The pages are compiled into the binary from `docs/cli/`; a unit test holds the table equal to the files there, so a page file not in the table (or a row with no file) fails the build's tests.

The verbs run before the tokio runtime and the daemon client are built: no daemon contact, no network, no child process. The pij shim forwards `docs` and `agents-start-here` to pij-rs unchanged (pij-native-verbs.json, RS_ROUTE_TABLE, the skill's verb table and pij-rs-api.md list them).

value.title: Docs verbs shipped
value.brief: One PR (#348, with PRD 009): docs.rs and its tests, the two verbs in main.rs, the start page, shim and skill wiring.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Verbs that own their grammar and help are clap subcommands with `disable_help_flag` and trailing args (`claim`, `directory`); the shim forwards the names in `harness/scripts/pij-native-verbs.json`, and `shim_forward_tests` (main.rs), `generation-routing.test.ts`, `generation-skill-coverage.test.ts` and `crates/cli/tests/skill_verb_coverage.rs` hold those lists, RS_ROUTE_TABLE and the skill's tables together. `main()` already handles `hook claude-display` before the runtime; the docs verbs go there too. The sibling ddocs CLI ships `agents-start-here` and `docs list/get` the same way.

value.risk: A page goes stale against the repo file it came from.
value.mitigation: The page is the file at build time; step s02 adds the check that the installed binary's page equals the file.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Cost: no loop, poll, timer, hook or launch. Each call is the existing shim start (one node, one pij-rs exec, as for `pij claim`) and an in-memory read of bytes in the binary; no file read, no daemon, no network. Scales with nothing: no per-seat or per-tick work.
Pages are public-safe: no customer or person names.
